title: Keeping the Darkness (AI) at bay
author: Uncled1023
selftext:
Hi ya'll,

I decided that I wanted to start making some developer posts about a game that I have been working on using Codex primarily.  It's finally at a place where I feel comfortable with the story and direction of the gameplay, so don't feel like i'd be sharing an all too different game than what I finally deliver.

I have been working on this for about the last 3 months pretty consistenty.  For me, I think the hard part wasn't the story, gameplay, or architecture (I'm a developer in my work so the coding isn't hard, just made faster with AI), but the art and audio. 

Some of the biggest issues I ran into were:

* Keeping the assets all thematically similar
* Avoiding that yellow tint
* Creating pixelated assets that are actually pixels, and not weird blobs

The big things that I did to combat this was:

* Created image generation scripts instead of having it generate the assets through the LLM
* Use the LLM to generate a "source" asset map so that i could nail down the style i wanted, and then modify the script to generate repeatable images that match/were close.
* When generating the assets, i had it do a bunch at a time to reduce drift and to be able to compare them all against each other.
* I didn't have it just assume everything was good and add the assets right away. After each step it required verification to help reduce the feedback loop, and then only promoted to the final build once i approved it all.  
* To prevent it accidentally changing things without my knowledge, there is a large validation pipeline that not only checks the general code quality, but compares the current build visually against previously promoted "baselines" pixel by pixel to ensure nothing drifted.  

As for gameplay and general development, it worked pretty well as long as i did it in bite sized chunks (Lo and behold, like actual development work) so that it 1) didn't have too much to think about and 2) allowed a faster feedback loop to catch issues and adjust.

If you'd like to take a gander at the steam page, it's here: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5060410/What_Iron_Cannot_Hold/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5060410/What_Iron_Cannot_Hold/)

I should have a beta/demo up fairly soon to allow others to stress and give feedback on the actual gameplay, cause no matter how it looks, if it doesn't play well, it won't be fun.
